methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multi-institutional (BC Cancer + MD Anderson) review of 75 urachal carcinomas over 1989–2023, with 28 SRCC vs 47 non-SRCC cases and dual pathologist case review. Analyses include Kaplan–Meier with log-rank and multivariate Cox (HR 3.38 for OS, 3.15 for CSS). Key weaknesses include the 34-year span introducing era-level heterogeneity (acknowledged), non-uniform pT staging due to mixed TURBT/biopsy/cystectomy specimens, unequal follow-up (mean 35.8 vs 62.1 months), and a borderline CSS p=0.053 interpreted as worse outcomes. Adjustment variables in the multivariate Cox model are not fully specified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Urachal SRCC is exceptionally rare (reported historically in scattered case reports), and a 28-case multi-institutional series is among the largest available, with direct clinical implications for staging, surgical approach, and adjuvant therapy decisions. The independent prognostic significance (HR ~3) is clinically meaningful. LoE is Oxford 4 (case series/low-quality cohort).

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-style reporting is partially present: design, setting, inclusion, IHC methods with antibody details, outcomes, and statistical methods. Limitations are acknowledged briefly. No STROBE checklist, no data sharing statement, and Table 1 is referenced but statistical comparison details between groups beyond a few p-values are limited. IHC analysis is performed on subsets without consistent denominator reporting for all markers.

novelty_literature.justification: Collecting 28 urachal SRCC cases in a two-center cohort is a meaningful extension given the rarity of the entity; prior literature is mostly single case reports and a recent NCDB analysis by Sakthivel et al. The work corroborates and modestly extends existing evidence but is not conceptually novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Clearly written with coherent structure, detailed Discussion contextualizing findings within the urachal carcinoma literature, and appropriate reference to consensus staging debates. Tables and figures are referenced. Minor issues include duplicated abstract-like sections and occasional inconsistencies in denominator reporting.

key_strengths: One of the largest multi-institutional urachal SRCC cohorts (n=28) with pathologist-validated classification
Clear independent prognostic effect of SRCC morphology on OS (HR=3.38) and CSS (HR=3.15)
Useful IHC characterization (CK20, CDX2, GATA3, beta-catenin) relevant for differential diagnosis
Contextualizes findings against NCDB and ISUP Dublin consensus discussions
key_concerns: 34-year inclusion span introduces era-based treatment heterogeneity
Non-uniform pT staging across TURBT, biopsy, and cystectomy specimens
Borderline CSS difference (p=0.053) and unequal follow-up between groups
Limited IHC subsets with variable denominators; MMR data in only 3 patients
No data availability statement and incomplete STROBE alignment
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically valuable rare-tumor series with consistent prognostic findings; the retrospective 34-year design and modest statistical depth fit a Tier 3 specialty pathology/oncology outlet after minor revisions.
